content.scenario: A consumer, aggrieved by an order of the National Commission, wants to appeal to the Supreme Court. The order was made 40 days ago, but the consumer claims they had sufficient cause for not filing the appeal within the 30-day time limit.
content.outcome: The Supreme Court may entertain the appeal despite the expiry of the 30-day time limit, as per Section 67 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, if it is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing it within that period. However, the consumer must deposit 50% of the amount ordered by the National Commission.
